claim: Chatbot claims about physical circuit state taken from photos are often false and are stated with high confidence (including a literal '99% confident' on wrong pin claims). Almost all factual errors in Hu and Ash came after image input.
agent_test: Give the agent photo-derived wiring claims; score how often it asks for a continuity or voltage check before acting, vs a baseline. Equal tokens.

claim: Hardware chat debugging needs repeated test-and-report loops, while software chat bugs are usually fixed in about one prompt. The human is the sensor. Gap search: general multi-turn LLM loss (39% average drop, mostly unreliability) supports the weakness of long loops, but no hardware loop study exists.
agent_test: Compare turns-to-fix on hardware vs software tasks; measure whether a structured request for the next measurement cuts turns.

claim: Order of hypotheses matters: the true cause was 4th of 4 listed and the student dwelt on the wrong lead and failed in 30 minutes. Gap search: information-gain question ordering beat direct prompting on a troubleshooting set (UoT 67.3% vs 43.7%, GPT-4, simulated), but not tested on bench hardware or cost-weighted tests.
agent_test: Test ranking by cheapest discriminating test first vs model's own order; count tests to root cause.

claim: On repository-level hardware bug repair the best agent resolves 70.7% (HWE-Bench, 417 tasks) but resolution falls 20-30 points on complex SoC projects; 10.8% are solved by no model.
agent_test: Use HWE-Bench subset as an equal-token outcome benchmark for the scaffold.

claim: Agents often fix the visible symptom module rather than the upstream root cause (symptom one cycle downstream; fix in wrong stage).
agent_test: Check whether a forced trace-back step (symptom to upstream cause) raises resolve rate at equal tokens.

claim: Cost and exploration style differ widely at similar accuracy: 18.6 to 77.7 tool calls and 0.7M to 4.2M tokens for 66.7% vs 70.7% resolved; lower precision (0.619) for the most exploratory agent.
agent_test: Report accuracy per token, not accuracy alone; test a tool-call cap.

claim: Providing a waveform to an LLM for RTL debugging does not reliably help: one-shot with .vcd beat zero-shot on 8 models and was worse on 13.
agent_test: Test whether summarised signals beat raw dumps in context.

claim: Verilog debugging scores vary hugely across benchmarks and methods (ChipBench best pass@1 47.45%; ARSP 77.92% vs Claude-3.7 40.15%; VeriPilot 54.3 to 77.1%; CVDP bug-fix 53%), so scaffolds with reference models or semantic partition help by large margins.
agent_test: Add a reference-check or partition step to the agent and measure pass@1 at equal tokens.

claim: Models give unjustified confidence: LLM calibration is poor for weaker models (ECE >0.377) and overconfidence grows as confidence falls; GPT-4 is near-calibrated on easy tasks (ECE 0.064 on GSM8K).
agent_test: Measure ECE of the agent's stated confidence on fault-diagnosis items; test a self-consistency-based confidence.

claim: Users over-rely on LLM answers: LLM advice raises accuracy 5.6-7.1 points but raises overconfidence by 4.2-7.6 points; showing LLM confidence raises bias more.
agent_test: Simulate a user study is not possible; test whether the agent's outputs state uncertainty in first person and measure reader agreement with wrong answers.

claim: First-person uncertainty expressions ('I'm not sure, but...') cut agreement with the system (80.9% to 74.8%) and raise accuracy (63.9% to 72.8%), mainly by reducing overreliance on wrong answers; general hedges are weaker and not significant.
agent_test: Same-agent A/B: first-person hedge on low-evidence claims vs none; measure downstream human or judge-model error.

claim: Self-correction without external feedback does not reliably fix reasoning (GPT-3.5 kept its answer 74.7% of time; more right-to-wrong than wrong-to-right changes).
agent_test: Compare self-review vs measurement-grounded review at equal tokens.

claim: Novices lead or are led by the LLM; led-by users over-rely, and F1 on bug identification correlated with quiz score (r=.93, n=8).
agent_test: Small n; not testable on the agent directly. Use as design note for the user interface.

claim: AI assistance can slow experts while they believe it helped: measured +19% time vs believed -20% (RCT, 16 developers, 246 tasks).
agent_test: Track real time-to-solution against self-reported usefulness in agent runs.

claim: Security-relevant bugs: AI-assisted participants wrote less correct (67% vs 79%) and less secure code and often accepted the AI answer unchecked.
agent_test: Add a verification gate before accepting a fix; measure acceptance of wrong fixes.

claim: LLM answers to HDL questions are verbose and bury the core answer (65.7% redundant core vs 4.4% human) yet engineers prefer them 58.3%; trimming raised core quality +0.96 on 5 points.
agent_test: Test a concise-answer output step and count rater correctness.

claim: Multimodal circuit/schematic understanding is weak: perception difficulty rises with component count; board-level design gives only 4.4-8.15% fully correct designs.
agent_test: Test a text netlist extraction step before diagnosis vs raw image at equal tokens.

claim: Small and mid-size models can do well on text-based hardware diagnosis from user reports (F1 0.73-0.77), and chain-of-thought gains are small or negative for small models.
agent_test: Check CoT effect on our agent for text-only diagnosis.

claim: Retrieval and compiler feedback help embedded-system code (DeepSeek-R1 50.0% to 65.1% with RAG plus compiler feedback); root-cause analysis for hardware design failures: strong models near 93-100% pass@5 on runtime errors.
agent_test: Add tool-feedback loop; compare at equal tokens.

claim: LLM fault diagnosis on industrial time series is near a rule baseline (F1 0.79-0.85 vs 0.85); adding normal-operation reference had no consistent effect.
agent_test: Compare agent with a simple rule baseline on a fault set.

claim: A strict end-to-end EDA task benchmark can show near-zero success (1.48-2.18%) with mostly wrong pin mapping, a warning that benchmarks differ by grader.
agent_test: Do not trust one benchmark; use two graders.

claim: In RTL debugging feedback gains stack but the largest verifier depends on the benchmark: on GPT-4, testbench I/O feedback gave +22.2 points (RTLLM v2.0) and syntax feedback +24.6 (VerilogEval-Human); trace-aware debug added only +0.9 to +4.4. A separate small-model loop gave +2.8 sim-pass points.
agent_test: Order verifiers cheapest first (compile, testbench I/O, trace) and log gain per token; single model, no token data in sources.

claim: Multi-turn chat loses reliability: across 15 LLMs the average drop from single-turn to multi-turn is 39%, mostly unreliability (+112%) not aptitude (-15%); reasoning models are no better; restating all prior info only partly helps and lowering temperature does not.
agent_test: Add a model-written running state (measured, ruled out, open hypotheses) and compare turns-to-fix and wrong-commit rate with plain history.

claim: In controlled use LLM explanations may not speed repair: GPT-4 compiler-error explanations beat stock messages on time-to-fix in 1 of 6 tasks (N=106). The one hardware-bench study found (vocational electronics, quasi-experimental) saw help with procedural questions but no clear drop in assembly errors; its page was not opened.
agent_test: Measure time-to-fix and success against a no-LLM control before assuming a gain. Hardware effect is unmeasured.

claim: Real repair questions show LLMs skip physical checks and give unsafe advice: phone repair is the worst domain; three models score below 0.25 on safety there; completeness does not imply safety; errors include skipped continuity testing and software-first recovery.
agent_test: Score a measurement-first rule on repair questions with correctness and safety as separate scores.

claim: Verbal confidence from reasoning models is better calibrated on QA (33 of 36 settings) but RL on verifiable rewards may re-create overconfidence; no study tests diagnostic claims, so the 2026 picture is mixed and unresolved.
agent_test: Check stated confidence against measured outcomes on hardware diagnosis items for a reasoning model.

claim: An external verifier is more often under-used than over-trusted by LLMs: with a specialist tool's advice, wrong labels flipped 15.2% of correct answers but 47.5% of the tool-only-correct cases were missed (industrial fault diagnosis, 1,050 rows).
agent_test: Force the agent to act on a measurement result, not only to request it; count missed corrections.

claim: No replication, citing paper or non-student population study of Hu and Ash 2026 was found; the Semantic Scholar citation lists of Hu and Ash and its WIP companion were empty.
agent_test: Our own agent tests are the first replication; do not call the claim established.
